$description: The Formats standard: how Plenix writes numbers, units, dates, money, percentages, names, addresses and phone numbers. platform/utils/format.ts applies it on the browser's Intl formatters (its FORMATS constant is this data; tests/formats.test.js keeps the two equal). Separators, symbol positions and date orders always come from the locale, never from here.

number.$description: Precision: the decimals a value gets when the caller does not fix them; keep one precision per column.

bytes.$description: File sizes in powers of 1000 with the Intl byte units (B, kB, MB, GB, TB).

relative.$description: Relative time ("5 minutes ago") for recent events; from this many days on, the absolute date.

currency.$description: Money shows the currency symbol; a page that mixes currencies shows the ISO 4217 code.

date.$description: The default date style: the month as text, never an all-numeric date.

address.$description: The order of a postal address's lines by country (ISO 3166 code). Field names: name, organization, street, locality, region, postalCode, country; the punctuation between two fields is written only when both have a value. The country line is shown when it differs from the reader's region.

phone.$description: Phone numbers are stored as E.164 (+ country code and number) and shown grouped by these patterns, keyed by the country calling code; # is one digit. A number whose length does not fit is shown in groups of three.
